Run those three commands in order; they cover (1) module-level A/B selection, (2) system-level candidate run, and (3) generating the next-fix report. Here’s what each does and what to look for.

## 1) Module autopilot: run + pick best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
- **Purpose:** Executes module-level experiments defined in `module_registry.yaml`, then **promotes the best-performing candidate** (per your selection rules) into the baseline/module set.
- **Expected output:** A run log plus an updated “best” selection; often this will update a “latest/champion” pointer or write a new artifact in `baseline/` or an experiment output directory (depends on your repo conventions).
- **Check after:** Confirm the “selected-best” actually updated the intended baseline artifact and didn’t fail any guardrails (min thresholds, regressions, etc.).

## 2) System autopilot: evaluate end-to-end system candidates
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
- **Purpose:** Runs full system candidates defined in `system_candidates.yaml` (end-to-end eval), typically slower but more representative.
- **Expected output:** A results table/log with key metrics (your handoff shows **tuning_mean/min** and **lockbox_mean/min** as primary).
- **Check after:** Identify any candidate that improves **lockbox_mean** without harming **lockbox_min** (often min is your safety metric), and verify tuning improvements aren’t overfitting.

## 3) Generate “next fix” recommendation report
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
- **Purpose:** Writes a prioritized debugging/next-actions report based on recent module experiment outcomes.
- **Expected output:** `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`
- **Check after:** Use it to decide what to try next if no candidate passes selection criteria or if improvements are only on tuning but not lockbox.

---

### If you want, paste the stdout/summary tables from steps (1) and (2)
I can help interpret which candidate (if any) should become the new champion given your tuning/lockbox mean+min constraints.
